title: Probe orthogonality + mini-dashboard sketch
content:
Context and purpose:

This is a compact working sketch to: 1) define a small set of mutually-orthogonal probes (signals) for token-serving inference, 2) map those probes to SLI/SLO candidates and trace anchors, and 3) propose a tiny ops dashboard (mini-dashboard) for fast investigation during bursts and rollout smoke-checks. Goal is to reduce operator context-switching and keep panels cheap to query.

Non-goals:
- Full signal catalog (this is intentionally narrow).
- Replacement for the main investigation dashboards.

High-level design constraints:
- Orthogonality: each probe should answer a single hypothesis (latency vs cost vs correctness).
- Low-cardinality: prefer cohort keys that keep query cardinality manageable (model_family, route, tenant_tier).
- Trace anchoring: every probe must have at least one span annotation pattern to link traces to the probe bucket.
- Cost cap: queries should be < 10s and cardinality limited for 1h windows.

Probe matrix (signal -> hypothesis -> short def -> SLI candidate -> trace anchor):

1) Fast-path TTFB probe
- Hypothesis: slow first-byte points to scheduling/placement or cold kernel issues.
- Short def: 95th percentile time_to_first_token (ms) for requests with seq_len <= 128 and cached_prefetch=false.
- SLI candidate: p95(ttfb) <= 120ms (can split by model_family).
- Trace anchor: span 'serving.runtime.generate' with tag kv_prefetch=false / placement_span_id.

2) KV-warmth tail probe
- Hypothesis: KV eviction causing long tails in per-token latency.
- Short def: fraction of requests with ==0kv_hits where expected_prefetch=true over 5m.
- SLI candidate: %zero_kv_hits_on-warm_segs <= 0.5% (tunable by tier).
- Trace anchor: span 'kv.service.lookup' with tag eviction=true or kv_miss_count>0.

3) Batching-pressure or queuing probe
- Hypothesis: high queue time or overly-large batches increasing p99.
- Short def: mean queue_time_ms and batch_size distribution for guarded routes (route.startsWith('/generate')).
- SLI candidate: p99(queue_time_ms) <= 30ms; median(batch_size) within expected range.
- Trace anchor: span 'scheduler.enqueue' / attribute batch_id.

4) Output-quality regression sentinel (cheap)
- Hypothesis: model regression detectable via simple heuristics (e.g., abrupt decline in keyword coverage).
- Short def: per-route ratio of requests with answer_length==0 or repeated-token streaks > 12.
- SLI candidate: sudden delta > 5% triggers review (not strict SLO).
- Trace anchor: span 'generation.output_checks' with hint flags.

5) Routing-fallback rate probe
- Hypothesis: frequent fallback indicates capacity shortages or compatibility issues.
- Short def: rate of requests that hit fallback route variant / total requests (1m window).
- SLI candidate: fallback_rate <= 0.2% for premium tenants; <=2% for free tier.
- Trace anchor: span attribute 'route.fallback=true' and original_route.

Metric definitions (compact, use consistent names):
- inference.request.count: count of user requests (string).
- inference.request.ttfb_ms: time from request received to first token emitted (ms).
- inference.token.latency_ms: per-token generation time for streaming tokens (ms).
- inference.kv.hits & inference.kv.misses: counts per request, used to compute kv_warmth.
- inference.scheduler.queue_time_ms: time spent waiting in scheduler queue.
- inference.batch.size: number of requests aggregated in batch.
- inference.fallback.count: count of requests served by fallback route.

Tagging guidance (keep small set):
- model_family (e.g., 'redwood-7b', 'llama2-13b')
- route (API path)
- tenant_tier (free|standard|premium|enterprise)
- region
- release_commit (short sha) 
- kv_prefetch_hint (true|false|unknown)

Tracing conventions (pragmatic):
- Span name shapes: service.operation e.g., serving.runtime.generate, scheduler.enqueue, kv.service.lookup, routing.resolve.
- Core attributes to emit on root span: request_id, model_family, route, tenant_tier, seq_len, batch_id (if any), release_commit.
- KV spans should emit kv_hit_count, kv_miss_count, eviction_flag (bool), prefetch_hint.
- Sampling: keep adaptive sampling so that any request that triggers a probe (e.g., high queue_time or fallback=true) is sampled at 100% for 10m after the event. Background sample: 0.1% of all requests, but ensure at-least-once-per-tenant-per-hour.
- Trace size guardrails: cap span_count <= 400; large traces should emit compact summary spans and drop verbose token-by-token spans unless debugging flag is set.

Mini-dashboard: panels and rationale (max 6 panels in single row view)
- Panel 1 (top-left): Key SLI tiles (p50/p95/p99 TTFB, kv_miss_rate, fallback_rate) - single-row numeric tiles with delta sparkline 1h. Purpose: operator immediate health check.
- Panel 2: Queue heatmap (time vs batch_size) for the last 2h - helps spot spikes in batching pressure.
- Panel 3: KV-warmth scatter: %0_kv_hits by model_family and tenant_tier for last 30m. Low-cardinality, explainable.
- Panel 4: Recent fallbacks table (top 20) with request_id, route, model_family, tenant_tier, fallback_reason. Click-through to trace.
- Panel 5: Trace anchor waterfall (example traces) — small sample seeded by adaptive sampler when any probe threshold breached.
- Panel 6 (optional): Cheap output-quality sentinel graph (ratio of zero-length answers or repeated-token streaks) with alert annotations.

Query/cost heuristics:
- Use pre-aggregated rollups for p99 and p95 where possible (1m rollups).
- Limit tag expansion to model_family+tenant_tier only for p99 queries in the dashboard.
- Back off dashboard live refresh to 30s when range > 2h.

Alerting and thresholds (starter suggestions):
- P95 TTFB > 200ms for 5m -> severity P2.
- KV miss_rate increase > 3x baseline over 10m -> P1 if accompanied by p99 token latency rise.
- Fallback rate > threshold (see probe matrix) sustained for 3m -> P1.
- Batch queue_time p99 > 200ms for 2m -> P2.

Operator playbook (compact):
1) Look at SLI tiles; if multiple tiles degraded, open the fallback table and kv scatter.
2) Use trace anchor waterfall to grab 3 example traces for the offending tenant/model.
3) Check recent deploys (release_commit tag) and active autoscale events.
4) If KV miss spike: check eviction logs and recent autoscaler churn. Warm caches via controlled synthetic probe (probe-runner endpoint).
5) If fallback spikes: verify routing policy, model compatibility matrix, and model capacity pools.

Instrumentation TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Add attribute release_commit to all root spans (ENG-OBS-xx).
- [ ] Emit kv_prefetch_hint on request ingestion path.
- [ ] Implement adaptive sampler hook to force-sample any request with queue_time_ms > 100ms.
- [ ] Create pre-aggregated p95/p99 rollups for ttfb and token.latency on 1m cadence.
- [ ] Add link target from fallback table rows to trace UI by request_id.

Open questions / design decisions:
- Where to compute kv_warmth metric best: at edge router (cheaper) vs model-side (more accurate)? Tradeoffs noted in linked artifacts.
- How aggressively should the adaptive sampler escalate sample rates for low-traffic tenants? We currently target at-least-once-per-tenant-per-hour but need to validate cost impact.
- Output-quality sentinels are heuristics—what alert cadence can we tolerate before too noisy? propose: only annotate, not page for now.

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Keep mini-dashboard free of > 3 tag dims. Focus on speed-to-insight.
- For rollouts: attach a temporary probe with tighter thresholds for 30m canary window.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS/mini-dashboard-canvas
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-3242 (adaptive sampler workstream)
- GitHub: PR #112 telemetry - adds kv_prefetch_hint

Last quick sketch: 2-row layout
Row A: SLI tiles | Queue heatmap | KV-warmth scatter
Row B: Recent fallbacks | Trace waterfall | Output-quality sentinel

If this looks reasonable I will: 1) sync with router team for fallback tags, 2) open the telemetry PRs for release_commit and kv_prefetch_hint, 3) prototype the dashboard with 1m rollups and test query cost in sandbox.

-- Ava
